title: Arduino and Circuit Foundations
description: Members set up Arduino Uno boards, identified their major components, and constructed introductory circuits while learning about voltage, current, resistance, power, Ohm’s law, and electrical safety.

title: Programmable LED Circuits
description: Students constructed LED circuits, selected appropriate resistors, and programmed Arduino boards to control electronic outputs.

title: Ultrasonic Distance-Sensing System
description: Students connected ultrasonic sensors to Arduino boards and used the resulting measurements to detect the distance of nearby objects.

title: Advanced Electronics Systems
description: Members experimented with transistors, DC motors, external power supplies, capacitors, and electronic displays. They learned how multiple components can be combined into larger physical systems.

title: Smart Physical Interaction Capstone
description: Students designed interactive electronic systems that detected environmental or user input and produced a physical or visual response. These projects integrated sensing, actuation, and feedback.

title: Arduino Programming and Troubleshooting
description: Members used introductory C++ programming to control components, read sensors, and correct wiring, coding, and component-related problems.

title: Multi-Component Electronic Systems
description: Students combined several electronic components to create larger systems that went beyond basic Arduino demonstrations.

title: Transistor and DC Motor Control
description: Members explored how transistors can control DC motors and other components that require more power than an Arduino pin can provide directly.

title: External Power and Capacitors
description: Students learned how external power supplies and capacitors can support larger and more reliable electronic systems.

title: Electronic Display Systems
description: Members integrated displays into their projects to present sensor readings, system information, and visual feedback.

title: Smart Physical Interaction System
description: Students designed interactive systems that detected environmental or user input, triggered a physical or visual response, and combined sensing, actuation, and feedback.

title: Self-Directed Electronics Projects
description: Students applied the skills developed throughout the program to projects aligned with their individual engineering interests.

title: Load-Bearing Bridge Challenge
description: Teams designed bridges using craft sticks, tape, and other basic materials before testing how much weight each structure could support.

title: Egg-Drop Challenge
description: Students created protective structures designed to prevent an egg from breaking when dropped.

title: Floating Boat Challenge
description: Teams designed and constructed boats capable of floating and carrying additional weight.

title: Spaghetti and Marshmallow Tower Challenge
description: Students competed to build the tallest stable tower using only spaghetti and marshmallows.

title: Rubber-Band Car Challenge
description: Teams designed and built rubber-band-powered vehicles before testing their creations in a racing competition.

title: Arduino Programming and Troubleshooting
description: Members used introductory C++ programming to control components, read sensors, and correct wiring, coding, and component-related problems.

title: Biomedical Sensor Lab
description: Students explored pulse, temperature, and MyoWare EMG sensors to understand how electronic systems collect signals from the human body.

title: Biological Signal Analysis
description: Members examined variation and noise in biological measurements and learned how filtering and data interpretation can improve the usefulness of sensor readings.

title: Human Monitoring and Response Capstone
description: Students combined biological sensors, data processing, and electronic outputs to create systems that measured a human-related signal and provided meaningful feedback.

title: Prosthetic and Assistive Technology Exploration
description: Members investigated how Arduino boards, muscle sensors, electronics, and programming can contribute to prosthetic and assistive technologies.
